title: Why grass is green: exercises
subtitle: Five exercises on the text
label: Exercises
review: Written by Claude from the lesson text. Check the English and the answers before using it with learners.

items.q: Plants use sunlight to make food.
Chlorophyll is a special red color.
Green light bounces back to our eyes.
What do plants need to live and grow?
items.why: “Plants need sunlight to live and grow.”

items.q: What is the special green color inside grass called?
Which light does grass use most?
items.why: “Grass uses mostly red and blue light.”

items.q: Where does the green light go?
options: It bounces back to our eyes
items.why: “The green light bounces back to our eyes.”

items.q: What is green the color of?
items.why: “Green is the color of healthy plants.”

blocks.title: 4. Open questions
blocks.note: These questions are open. Talk about your answers with your teacher or a classmate.

items.q: Without looking at the text, sum it up in three sentences.
items.model: Grass is a plant, and it uses sunlight to make food. It has a green color inside it called chlorophyll. Grass uses mostly red and blue light, and the green light bounces back to our eyes.

items.q: Which colors of light does grass use? Which color does it not use much?
items.model: It uses mostly red and blue light. It does not use much green light.

items.q: Why are many trees and bushes green too?
Name three green plants you can see near your home or school.

blocks.title: 5. Put in order
blocks.intro: Put the ideas in the order of the text.
items: Plants use sunlight to make food
Grass uses mostly red and blue light
Green light bounces back to our eyes
